findings.title: Table public.test_apply lacks a Primary Key constraint
findings.current_behavior: Table has no declared primary key constraint in pg_constraint.
findings.why_it_is_a_problem: Prevents logical replication, impairs row identification in ORMs, causes sequential scans on single-row updates/deletes, and compromises data integrity.
findings.recommended_change: Add a primary key constraint to public.test_apply (typically on an id UUID or composite business key).
findings.suggested_sql: ALTER TABLE public.test_apply ADD PRIMARY KEY (id);
findings.expected_benefit: Enables fast index-based lookups, logical replication compatibility, and strict row uniqueness.
findings.implementation_risk: LOW - Existing duplicate rows would cause the ALTER command to fail until deduped.
findings.testing_requirements: Verify table contents for duplicates before applying constraint.
findings.rollback_considerations: ALTER TABLE public.test_apply DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS test_apply_pkey;

findings.title: Missing Index on Foreign Key: public.billing_payment_ledger.plan_id
findings.current_behavior: Foreign key constraint billing_payment_ledger_plan_id_fkey references plans.id, but no supporting B-tree index exists on plan_id.
findings.why_it_is_a_problem: Deletions or updates on referenced parent table require a FULL SEQUENTIAL SCAN of the child table to verify foreign key integrity, creating massive disk I/O and shared lock contention.
findings.recommended_change: Create a supporting B-tree index on public.billing_payment_ledger(plan_id).
findings.suggested_sql: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_billing_payment_ledger_plan_id ON public.billing_payment_ledger(plan_id);
findings.expected_benefit: Eliminates sequential scans during parent deletes/updates and accelerates JOIN queries.
findings.implementation_risk: LOW - CONCURRENTLY avoids locking production writes.
findings.testing_requirements: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) query joining parent and child.

findings.title: 1 SECURITY DEFINER functions lack explicit search_path
findings.current_behavior: 1 functions execute with elevated superuser/owner privileges without an immutable search_path.
findings.why_it_is_a_problem: Critical privilege escalation vulnerability (CWE-426): an authenticated attacker can create temporary tables or operators in their schema and hijack function execution flow.
findings.recommended_change: Alter all SECURITY DEFINER routines to pin search_path = public, pg_temp.
findings.suggested_sql: ALTER FUNCTION <func_signature> SET search_path = public, pg_temp;
findings.expected_benefit: Completely eliminates search_path hijacking in multi-tenant environment.
findings.implementation_risk: LOW - Standard Supabase security hardening recommendation.
findings.testing_requirements: Execute function as authenticated role and verify search_path isolation.

findings.title: Monolithic High-Velocity Table: public.emails lacks Partitioning
findings.current_behavior: Table public.emails is an append-heavy operational log / queue stored as a single monolithic table.
findings.why_it_is_a_problem: As records accumulate, index sizes exceed available shared_buffers, autovacuum incurs high read/write amplification, and data retention deletions require expensive DELETE sweeps.
findings.recommended_change: Implement PostgreSQL 17 Declarative Range Partitioning by RANGE (created_at) with monthly partition intervals.
findings.suggested_sql: CREATE TABLE public.emails_partitioned (...) PARTITION BY RANGE (created_at);
findings.expected_benefit: Enables partition pruning (10x faster range queries), instant zero-downtime data archival via DROP TABLE, and localized index maintenance.
findings.implementation_risk: MEDIUM - Requires migration with composite primary key: PRIMARY KEY (id, created_at).
findings.testing_requirements: Validate ORM compatibility with composite PK on staging environment.
findings.rollback_considerations: Revert writes to original unpartitioned table.
